title: Implement token-bucket fairness for shared burst pools (WFQ hybrid)
author: Jordan Lee
description:
Context
We need strict, explainable fairness enforcement for Redwood-managed shared burst pools so that a single tenant (or a small set) cannot monopolize burst capacity and degrade neighbors. This PR implements the fairness mechanism selected in ADR: a token-bucket + WFQ hybrid suitable for admission-time decisions with deterministic outcomes, plus tests and a small simulation harness.

What this PR does
- Adds per-tenant burst fairness accounting in the Burst Admission Controller.
- Implements a weighted token bucket (WTB) for each tenant + pool, with:
  - refill_rate = weight * pool_fair_share (derived from configured priority tier + baseline)
  - burst_size = configurable max_credit_seconds (prevents long idle tenants from accumulating unbounded credit)
  - charge = admitted_burst_gpu_seconds (estimated) at decision time
- Adds a WFQ-style tie-breaker for queued requests when multiple tenants are simultaneously eligible:
  - each admitted request is assigned a virtual finish time based on tenant weight
  - scheduler selects the minimum virtual finish time among eligible tenants
  - ensures stable ordering under contention, reduces oscillation vs pure token bucket
- Introduces anti-starvation guardrails:
  - min_grant_interval (bounded waiting time for low-weight tenants when pool has any headroom)
  - max_consecutive_admits_per_tenant under saturation to avoid head-of-line domination
- Explicitly separates two signals:
  - fairness eligibility (this PR)
  - fleet safety / circuit breaker (out of scope here; tracked in ENG-4902)

Determinism notes
Admission decisions must be deterministic for a given snapshot to prevent routing thrash and retry storms. This PR:
- Computes all decisions using a single "decision_time" passed from the caller (gateway/router) and uses monotonic time only within the controller.
- Avoids reading "now" multiple times within the decision path.
- Makes refill a pure function of (last_update, decision_time).
- Adds rounding rules for charges/refills (ceil to 10ms) to keep floating point drift out of comparisons.

Implementation overview
- New package: services/burst-admission-controller/fairness
  - TokenBucket: credit_seconds, last_update, refill_rate_seconds_per_second, max_credit_seconds
  - FairnessStateStore: in-memory implementation for tests + interface for the production backing store (redis-like) used elsewhere in the service
  - WfqScheduler: maintains per-tenant virtual time and calculates finish times for each admitted request
- New config surface (wired through existing controller config struct; policy engine wiring in separate PR):
  - fairness.enabled (default false)
  - fairness.max_credit_seconds (default 30s)
  - fairness.min_grant_interval (default 2s)
  - fairness.max_consecutive_admits (default 8)
  - fairness.weight_map (tier -> weight; e.g., gold=4, silver=2, standard=1)

Illustrative snippet (fairness charge)
- Before: admission checked only pool-level saturation + per-tenant cap
- After: admission also requires sufficient tenant credit

Pseudo-code (actual code is Go; simplified here):
  bucket = loadBucket(tenant,pool)
  bucket.refill(decisionTime)
  cost = estimateBurstGpuSeconds(req)
  if bucket.credit < cost: deny(FairnessInsufficientCredit)
  if saturated: enqueueWithFinishTime(req, wfq.finishTime(tenant,cost))
  else: bucket.credit -= cost; admit()

Simulation harness
Adds tools/fairness-sim (Go) to run a discrete-event simulation over synthetic tenant traffic patterns:
- scenarios: 1 bully tenant + 9 normal, 3 gold tenants + 20 standard, thundering herd at top of minute
- outputs: per-tenant admitted share, avg wait, p95 wait, starvation events
- results (local, deterministic seed):
  - bully scenario: bully share capped at ~weight/(sum weights) within ~10s; no starvation events observed
  - herd scenario: lower p95 wait variance vs pure token bucket; fewer oscillations in admit/deny patterns

Tests
- Unit tests covering:
  - refill math + rounding invariants
  - max_credit_seconds cap
  - fairness denial reason codes
  - WFQ ordering stability under equal weights
  - anti-starvation: low-weight tenant gets admitted within min_grant_interval when pool has headroom
- Property-ish test (bounded randomized) asserting:
  - over N seconds under sustained contention, share error <= 8% from ideal weighted share

Observability (minimal in this PR)
- Adds internal debug counters (not yet exported as Prometheus metrics; those are in PR-23822):
  - fairness_admit_total
  - fairness_deny_insufficient_credit_total
  - fairness_enqueue_total
  - fairness_starvation_prevented_total

Rollout / safety
- Feature-gated behind fairness.enabled.
- No behavior change when fairness.enabled = false.
- Backward compatible with existing tenant configs.

Follow-ups
- Wire fairness config via policy engine rules (PR-24033).
- Export Prometheus metrics + dashboards (PR-23822 / observability-pack).
- Validate at scale with load test harness (ENG-4841).

Refs
- ADR: adr-fairness-model-for-shared-burst-pools
- Related: ENG-4810 (controller skeleton), ENG-4821 (fairness enforcement)

Release notes
- Dedicated Burst: admission controller can enforce weighted fairness across tenants sharing a burst pool (feature-flagged).

review_conversation: Keiko Yamamoto: Can we cap accumulated credits? Otherwise an idle tenant could come back and monopolize the pool for minutes. Also please add a test around the cap behavior.
Jordan Lee (author): +1. Added fairness.max_credit_seconds (default 30s) and tests (TokenBucket_CapsCredit).
Mina Haddad: Routing needs deterministic denials for retries. Please confirm we don’t call time.Now() multiple times and that rounding is stable across instances.

Jordan Lee (author): Updated decider to pass decision_time through the call chain; refill/charge are pure functions of that timestamp. Also added 10ms rounding to avoid drift; see Fairness_RoundingInvariant test.
Ethan Park: The WFQ piece worries me if we don’t persist virtual time across controller instances. What happens on restart?

Jordan Lee (author): We persist (per-tenant virtual_time, last_finish) in the same state store record as the bucket; in-memory store is for tests only. Added a restart test using store reload to ensure monotonicity.
Sean Gallagher: Please add an explicit anti-starvation knob and a metric/counter for when it triggers. We’ll want to alert on pathological cases in beta.
Jordan Lee (author): Added fairness.min_grant_interval + fairness_starvation_prevented_total counter; metrics export will land in PR-23822.
Allison Grant: Label/cardinality: please don’t include raw tenant_id in any exported metrics. OK to keep internal debug counters for now, but follow-up must be careful.
Jordan Lee (author): Agree. This PR only adds internal counters with tenant_id in structured logs (debug-level) behind redaction. Metrics export PR will use tier/pool only.
merge_outcome: Merged to main after 5 approvals; feature remains disabled by default via fairness.enabled.
